# Armenia formation and regime-planning source record

Read on 24 October 2026 for the formation, tax-overview and tax-planning Guides. This is a targeted source record, not a full review of Armenian corporate, AML, tax-procedure or sectoral law. Current Armenian texts control. The current English Tax Code translation was used only as a supporting translation and checked against the Armenian Code for the provisions used below.

## Primary texts read

| Source | URL | Relevant provisions read |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Law on State Registration of Legal Entities, current Armenian text | https://www.arlis.am/hy/acts/218933 | Articles 1, 17, 34, 35 and 60.1–60.3 |
| Law on Limited Liability Companies, current Armenian text | https://www.arlis.am/hy/acts/207710/latest | Articles 1, 3, 8–11, 28–30, 34, 36–37; checked the effective-date note for the 2027 Article 1 amendment |
| Armenian Tax Code, current Armenian text | https://www.arlis.am/hy/acts/215611/latest | Articles 30, 103, 125, 150, 253–270; targeted activity, rate, expense and filing provisions |
| Armenian Tax Code, official English translation | https://www.arlis.am/en/acts/231892 | Supporting translation for the Tax Code provisions; Armenian current text controls |

## Formation claims retained

- The registration application includes the founding decision or minutes, charter, proof of state-duty payment and executive-head details. Foreign individual founder identity documents and foreign legal-founder evidence have certification and Armenian-translation requirements. Special entity laws can add documents. Registration Law Article 34.
- Paper and online filing are provided for. Ordinary registration is due no later than one working day after complete documents; two working days applies if a founder is a legal person. The applicant can request up to 30 calendar days. Immediate registration is limited to the distinct Article 17(9)–(10) filing route. Registration Law Articles 17 and 35.
- Registration assigns a registration number, taxpayer account number and social-payment account number. The entity exists from registration. Registration Law Article 35.
- The LLC Law sets no general minimum capital but allows special laws to set sector-specific minimums. It allows non-cash contributions, requires unanimous participant valuation and an independent appraiser over the statutory 500-fold threshold. Contributions are due by the founders' agreement deadline, no later than one year from registration. The AMD value of the appraisal threshold was deliberately not stated; the statutory salary basis was not reconciled to a current AMD value for this Guide. LLC Law Articles 28–30.
- An LLC may have no more than 49 participants under the general rule. LLC Law Article 11.
- The annual results meeting is held once yearly, no earlier than two months and no later than six months after year-end. LLC Law Article 37. It approves the annual report and balance sheet under Article 36.
- Registered legal persons must identify and maintain beneficial-owner information, conduct periodic due diligence at least annually, file an initial declaration within 40 days of registration, promptly report changes (within 40 days after the company learns of them at the latest), and confirm or update data by 20 February annually. Registration Law Articles 60.1–60.3. The underlying beneficial-owner criteria are in the AML Law, which was not read for this record; no percentage test is asserted.

## Tax-planning claims retained

- Ordinary resident-company profit tax is generally 18%; the Code has special taxpayer and tax-base rules. Article 125.
- Article 253 distinguishes resident commercial organisations from individual entrepreneurs: the turnover-tax regime substitutes for profit tax and/or VAT for a qualifying organisation; for an individual entrepreneur it substitutes for VAT. Article 125(3) separately sets AMD 5,000 monthly profit tax for the specified turnover-regime entrepreneur case. This does not make either regime universally available.
- The turnover-tax threshold is prior-year sales not exceeding AMD 115 million; the micro-business threshold is prior-year sales not exceeding AMD 24 million. Existing annual and new-registration statements use different dates, including the 20th day after registration. Articles 254 and 267.
- The turnover-tax exclusion includes specified regulated activity and activity classes 69, 70, 78.2 and 78.3. The micro-business exclusions are separately enumerated and broader. Articles 254(3)–(3.1) and 267(3)–(5). Full aggregation, classification and exit rules were not exhaustively reconstructed.
- Article 258 rates used in the Guide: 10% ordinary trade; 5% listed secondary raw-material trade; 1.5% newspaper editorial sales; 7% production; 10% rent, interest and royalties; 12% catering; 20% specified other catering-taxpayer income; 1% government-listed high-technology activity; 10% other assets including immovable property; and 10% other activity. The high-technology row is effective through 31 December 2031. The current Government activity list was not read, so no activity is represented as qualifying for that rate.
- For the specified trade, production, catering and other-activity branches, Article 258 permits expense reductions at 9.5%, 5%, 9% and 6%, with respective tax-base floors of 1%, 3%, 3.5% and 4.5%. It restricts deductible documentation and expense categories, permits qualifying unused reductions to carry forward, and Article 260 requires separate records or proportional allocation for specified shared administrative and sales expenses.
- Articles 261–262 set quarterly turnover-tax return and payment dates by the 20th of the next month. Article 270 sets a 1 February annual turnover report for covered micro-business taxpayers and retains separate withholding/exception reporting.

## Deliberately unresolved

The Guide does not state an incorporation-fee amount or fee waiver. The state-duty amount for the selected formation route was not verified. The end-to-end online identification route, statutory-minimum-salary base for the LLC appraisal threshold, current AML beneficial-owner test, full Article 254 aggregation and regime-exit rules, complete Article 267/Annex 3 activity classification, high-technology list, current forms and portal, and sector-specific formation rules remain open. # Armenia LLC formation and first compliance steps v0.2

## When this guide applies

This guide covers an ordinary Armenian limited liability company (LLC) formed under the general company and registration laws. Banks, insurers, investment businesses, crypto-asset service providers and other regulated activities have separate rules. A registration certificate does not establish that a regulated activity, work permit, residence status, tax regime, bank account or licence is available. Check the activity and founders before choosing the route. [Registration Law, Article 1](https://www.arlis.am/hy/acts/218933); [LLC Law, Article 1](https://www.arlis.am/hy/acts/207710/latest)

## Form and founder route

An LLC is a commercial legal person with separate property. It may be established by one or more natural or legal persons. An LLC may generally have no more than 49 participants; if the number rises above 49, the company must reorganise within one year or face the statutory consequences. Special-sector companies need separate review. [LLC Law, Articles 3, 8 and 11](https://www.arlis.am/hy/acts/207710/latest)

The registration application includes the founding decision or meeting minutes, charter, proof of state-duty payment, and identifying details and email for the executive head. A sole founder supplies a written sole-founder decision. A foreign individual founder supplies a certified copy of a passport or equivalent identity document with Armenian translation. A foreign-company founder supplies a certified and Armenian-translated register extract or equivalent proof of legal status and its founding documents. Special laws can require more. [Registration Law, Article 34](https://www.arlis.am/hy/acts/218933)

Applications may be submitted in person on paper or through the information system. The ordinary statutory decision period is no later than one working day after complete documents are submitted. It is two working days if any founder is a legal person. A commercial applicant can request a longer period up to 30 calendar days. Immediate registration is available only through the specific identification and filing routes in Article 17(9)–(10); it is not a general promise of same-day registration. The Register assigns the registration and tax numbers and the social-payment account number when it records the new legal person. [Registration Law, Articles 17 and 35](https://www.arlis.am/hy/acts/218933)

The law requires evidence of state-duty payment, but this guide does not state a fee amount or exemption. Check the current state-duty rule and the chosen filing route before budgeting. Registration documents do not guarantee a bank will open an account. [Registration Law, Articles 3 and 34](https://www.arlis.am/hy/acts/218933); [LLC Law, Article 3](https://www.arlis.am/hy/acts/207710/latest)

## Capital, charter and management

The LLC Law sets no general minimum charter capital; another law can set a sector-specific minimum. The charter states the company name, registered office, capital and share details, and founder information. Non-cash contributions are permitted. Participant approval of their value is unanimous; an independent appraiser is required where a contribution's nominal value exceeds the statutory 500-fold threshold. Contributions must be paid by the founders' agreement deadline, no later than one year after state registration. Check the current statutory salary basis before applying the valuation threshold; this guide does not convert it into an AMD amount. [LLC Law, Articles 10 and 28–30](https://www.arlis.am/hy/acts/207710/latest)

The LLC is created when the state registration is made. Its registered office is tied to the location of its permanently operating executive body under the LLC Law. The law provides for an executive body; it does not support a blanket claim here that every foreign-owned LLC can operate without a resident director or local work authorisation. Resolve the actual director, immigration and regulated-sector facts separately. [LLC Law, Articles 3, 8 and 10](https://www.arlis.am/hy/acts/207710/latest)

## Tax registration and first filings

Company registration is not the end of tax setup. A newly registered company that seeks turnover-tax status generally must submit its statement by the 20th day following registration; the micro-business statement has its own 20-day deadline and activity/eligibility conditions. Eligibility is not automatic. See [Armenia tax planning](armenia-tax-optimization.md) before selecting a regime. [Tax Code, Articles 254 and 267](https://www.arlis.am/hy/acts/215611/latest)

An Armenian-registered legal person must identify and keep reliable information about its actual beneficial owners. The initial declaration is due within 40 days after registration. Changes must be declared promptly and no later than 40 days after the company learns of them. By 20 February each year, the company must confirm that the latest declaration remains current as at 31 December or submit updated data. Beneficial-owner identification follows the Anti-Money Laundering Law; the registration law does not itself define a universal ownership-percentage test. [Registration Law, Articles 60.1–60.3](https://www.arlis.am/hy/acts/218933)

The annual results meeting must be held at least once a year and within two to six months after the financial year ends. The general meeting approves the annual report and balance sheet and decides on profit distribution within the statutory limits. This is a shareholder-meeting deadline, not a substitute for tax filings or any separate accounts-preparation requirement. [LLC Law, Articles 36–37](https://www.arlis.am/hy/acts/207710/latest)

## Items to confirm for a real formation

Confirm the actual activity and licences; founder identity and document certification; registered office and director; state-duty amount; accepted online identification route; applicable tax-regime filing; beneficial-owner analysis under AML rules; accounting and financial-statement rules; and immigration or employment permissions. This guide does not confirm a filing acceptance, fee, bank account, permit or professional sign-off.

# Armenia corporate income tax preparation v0.2

## Who this applies to

Prepare ordinary resident-company and registered corporate-PE profit-tax workpapers for tax year 2026. Resident organisations are located in Armenia under the statutory registration test; resident corporate income includes domestic and foreign objects, while PE attribution and no-PE/non-attributed receipts have separate rules. This is not the individual entrepreneur's 23% method, the investment-fund net-assets method or a certification of special-regime eligibility. [Code Articles 20, 22–23, 103–105, 125][code]; [cross-border method](am-cross-border.md)

Establish the regime for each period before computing 18% profit tax. Article 254's ordinary turnover-tax gate includes prior-year turnover not exceeding AMD 115 million, timely declaration and exclusions, including specified legal/accounting, head-office/management and labour-supply activities. Article 267's micro gate includes AMD 24 million and extensive activity/person/relationship exclusions. Equal-to and less-than are not interchangeable. Do not treat a small turnover, broad label such as IT, or the old formation/planning summary as an election. Current activity codes, linked-person aggregation, transition dates, declarations and full rate/deduction schedules remain to be implemented before recommending either regime. [254–255, 267–268][code]

## Rates, bands and thresholds

| Item | Amount or period | Tax year and primary source |
|---|---|---|
| Ordinary corporate / attributable corporate-PE tax | 18% of established taxable profit | 2026, [125(1)][code] |
| Representation, established business | Up to 0.5% of annual gross income, capped at AMD 5 million | 2026, [116][code] |
| Representation, registration year | Separate AMD 5 million limit; ordinary percentage restriction does not apply | 2026, [116(2)][code] |
| General qualifying charitable deductions | Up to 0.25% of annual gross income | 2026, [123(1)(5)][code] |
| Specified licensed state/community education/foundation recipients | Separate qualifying category up to 2.5% | 2026, [123(1)(5.1)][code] |
| Small depreciable asset original cost | Up to AMD 50,000 inclusive, full acquisition-year deduction | 2026, [121(2)(1)][code] |
| Ordinary loss carryforward | Five tax years following origin year, with ordering/regime/reorganisation restrictions | 2026, [123(1)(4)][code] |
| Quarterly instalment | Lower of adjusted prior-year tax × 20% and defined prior-quarter income × 2%, after exceptions | 2026, Armenian [135][code] |

The English instalment sentence is ambiguous. The Armenian Article 135(1) expressly uses the minimum of the two calculated amounts. It is not a 2%-of-revenue floor, and no old March election should be invented after paragraph 4's repeal. Other English passages, including an exceptional historical asset-period wording, need Armenian verification before use. [135, 121][code]; [English reproduction][english]

HO-234-N restates representation and changes other base rules from its specified dates. Use its July 2026 gate with the actual period. HO-385-N's general February 2027 bank-dividend provisions are not October 2026 ordinary corporate rates; its specified expense amendment has a different commencement. Do not apply all provisions of an enacted law on publication without checking the transition. [HO-234-N, especially 23–25 and commencement][july]; [HO-385-N 14][future]

## The base

### Reconcile accounts to tax once

Start with complete accrual accounts and a gross-income ledger under Articles 104–109, then distinguish tax inclusion/exclusion, timing and deductions. A practical book-profit bridge adds back non-deductible amounts and book depreciation, deducts permitted tax depreciation and other legal deductions, and reconciles to the statutory gross-income-minus-deductions result. Do not deduct a cost twice through both inventory and overhead, or treat every cash payment as a current expense. [105–106, 108–111, 121][code]

Article 111 requires the prescribed supporting documents, subject to express exceptions. Article 121(7) matches production/trading costs to supplied goods/work/services or disposals; administrative/selling/financial expenses have their stated tax-year and capitalisation rules. Preserve contract, actual transaction date, invoice, receipt, inventory and asset evidence. An invoice date in another year does not alone decide the service expense period. [55, 111, 121(7)][code]

Articles 112–113 exclude or restrict categories including equity distributions/investments, specified revaluations, public-budget/tax sanctions, costs associated with excluded income, creditable indirect taxes and expenses beyond statutory caps. **Not all fines are the same:** Article 113(1)(1) disallows its public/pension/tax-controlled sanctions, while Article 121(8)(5) separately addresses other monetary sanctions. Do not automatically disallow a private contractual compensation or deduct a tax penalty. [112–113, 121(8)][code]

Supplier regime matters. Article 113(1)(8) restricts the stated micro-entrepreneurship purchases; paragraph (10) separately restricts listed high-technology activities purchased from turnover taxpayers. Validate supplier and activity at transaction date. This is not a blanket statement that every turnover-tax supplier invoice is nondeductible. No unsupported invoice-to-bank match proves statutory deductibility. [113][code]

### Capped costs and evidence

Representation means the stated cooperation-establishment/maintenance costs, not every travel, advertising or customer expense. Retain purpose and recipient evidence before applying the gross-income percentage/absolute cap. Article 117 foreign travel has its own 5%-of-gross-income rule, registration-year and documented overseas work/service exceptions, plus daily/other limits. Do not use the representation cap for travel or invent a current per-diem schedule. [116–117][code]

Article 120 has separate employee accommodation/benefit conditions and assistance/food/social-cost limits; Article 119 voluntary pension limits are separate from mandatory payroll contributions. Donation deductions under Article 123 require actual recipient-category evidence and valuation; the special 2.5% category is not every educational or charitable payment. Track each legal deduction without counting it again as an ordinary expense. Detailed per-diem, accommodation, health/pension benefit and subsidy implementation remains open. [119–120, 123][code]

### Interest

Article 114 applies a per-loan interest-rate limitation based on twice the **31 December** CBA bank-interest settlement rate, not whichever monetary-policy rate a website displays today. The final 31 December 2026 input is not established on this October read. The example below deliberately uses a hypothetical established closing rate. Obtain the actual official rate for the tax year before final computation. [114(1)(1)][code]

For borrowings from nonbank/noncredit providers, Article 114(1)(2) separately limits the annual interest amount to twice positive closing tax equity for ordinary taxpayers, or nine times for the stated bank/credit population. Negative equity has the stated disallowance consequence; listed international-development/public debt-placement exceptions need evidence. This provision compares **interest amounts** with the equity-based amount; do not silently substitute a debt-to-equity principal ratio. [114(1)(2)][code]

Interest-free/low-yield onward lending and capitalised borrowing costs have additional rules in Article 114(1)(3)–(4). Record time, maximum relevant borrowing rates and overlap so the same disallowance is not added twice. A TP-supported rate does not override Article 114 or prove the business expense deductible. Complex portfolios, zero equity and exceptions require further implementation; the single-loan control assumes none applies. [114, 121(7)(5)][code]; [TP method](am-transfer-pricing.md)

### Tax depreciation and capital expenses

Ordinary minimum terms under Article 121(1)(3):

| Statutory asset group | Minimum years | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Ordinary buildings/structures and stated linear infrastructure | 20 | [121(1)(3), row 1][code] |
| Specified hotel/guest-house/sanatorium/education buildings | 10 | [row 2][code] |
| Production equipment | 5 | [row 3][code] |
| Conveyors/robotic technology | 3 | [row 4][code] |
| Computer/computational and communication equipment | 1 | [row 5][code] |
| Other fixed assets | 8 | [row 6][code] |

Use per-asset original cost/selected lawful term, with different rules for statutory revaluation and changed terms. Terms can be longer, not shorter than the applicable minimum absent an actual exception. Intangibles use the established possible-use period; where it cannot be determined, the statutory ten-year rule and taxpayer-life limit apply. Small assets up to 50,000 inclusive have a separate immediate-deduction rule. Do not extend a historic acquisition-window incentive to an ordinary 2026 purchase. [121(1)–(2)][code]

For ordinary acquisition/disposal/status changes, full months use annual deduction × months/12 and incomplete months use the separately stated annual deduction × days/365. Do not round every commencement up to a full month. The worked case uses six complete months and no incomplete period. Asset nonbusiness/leased status, land, useful-life changes, revaluations and different methods for specialised assets need their own statutory route. [121(1)(6)][code]

Capital improvements have per-asset original-value 5% and cumulative 15% tests and capitalisation/revised-period rules in Article 121(3). Do not expense a refurbishment simply because its accounting label is repairs. Leased/gratuitous-use property, missing original/book values, land improvements, end-of-lease balances and R&D require the actual contract and special method; no general immediate write-off is certified here. [121(3)–(6)][code]

### Losses, bad debts and incentives

Calculate current-year expenses/losses first, then eligible prior losses oldest first within five following tax years. General-system losses do not stop aging while the taxpayer uses a special regime; losses generated in that special regime are not ordinary carryforwards. Division/separation/consolidation/absorption have explicit different rules; neither all succession nor all forfeiture is automatic. Retain origin-year tax returns, use, expiry, corrections and regime/reorganisation history. [123(1)(4)][code]

Book impairments are not automatically tax bad debts. Article 123's government-rule route and over-AMD-300,000 legal-enforcement conditions need the operative reserve/write-off instrument and actual judicial/notarial/arbitral event. Asset/inventory losses under Article 122 require classification, documentation and relevant norms/events. These detailed methods remain open, not replaced by an accountant's estimate. [122–123][code]

Resident dividends and enhanced disability/technology/R&D deductions have separate statutory provisions. Technology/R&D benefits require current activity/occupation lists, status/commission evidence, applicable date and base caps; no automatic deduction is granted merely because a company develops software. Specific banks/funds, mining, agriculture, films, border-area and other relief need dedicated implementation. Future bank-dividend rules must be reconciled separately. [123–127][code]; [HO-385-N][future]

## Deadlines and filing

The ordinary annual resident/PE profit-tax return and payment are due by 20 April inclusive of the following tax year under Articles 134(1)/136(1). Thus the statutory date for 2026 is 20 April 2027, before separately established calendar adjustments/extensions. Quarterly advances are due by the 20th of the quarter's last month. Keep annual tax, advances calculated/paid, credits and the authority ledger separate. [130–136][code]

For each advance, compute the lower of 20% of **adjusted** prior-year tax and 2% of Article 135's defined prior-quarter supply/work/service income. The prior-tax limb excludes the listed special-regime, relief, non-attributed PE, foreign-tax and audit amounts; the income limb uses the specified VAT/excise-return bases submitted by the advance deadline, with rules for later corrections. The new prior-year return affects the next advance under paragraph 2.1; paragraph 3 supplies the pre-filing fallback. Do not substitute accounting turnover or divide an annual liability by four. [135(1)–(3)][code]

Paragraphs 5–8 address registration year, VAT-status changes, a later authority finding, properly declared inactivity and different reorganisations. Do not turn these into a blanket no-advance election. Keep the declaration and dates; an inactive bank account is not an inactivity filing. [135(5)–(8)][code]

The actual 749-N **July 2026 consolidation**, not its earlier 2018–2024 text, provides Annex 1 for ordinary resident/PE profit tax. Prepare a positive-value workpaper and deliberately translate deductions into the form's parenthesised/sign convention. [749-N Annex 1 and instructions][return]

## Penalties and interest

Current Article 401 ordinarily charges 0.075% late-payment interest per day, with its 730-day maximum/scope. Article 402 charges 5% of calculated tax for each completed 15-day late-return interval subject to its stop rules and cap at calculated tax. Article 403 provides ordinary under-declaration sanctions of 50%, and 100% for the specified recurrence, with exceptions. Classify actual offence, original due date, correction and assessment before combining amounts. Private contractual damages are a separate deduction question. [401–403][code]

Full amended-return relief, administrative offences, service/audit/appeal/suspension, interest interaction and enforcement need actual procedural evidence. No guessed appeal period, penalty waiver or filing-extension payment holiday. [54, 401–403][code]

## Worked examples that recompute

Hypothetical AMD, ordinary established 2026 corporate scope, no unmentioned relief or competing credits. Inputs described as eligible/allowable require their own evidence.

### 1. Book-to-tax bridge and annual balance

Book profit 30 million already includes public tax fine 500,000 and book depreciation 3 million. Add them back; replace with established tax depreciation 4 million. Current tax result 29.5 million; eligible prior loss 5 million leaves taxable profit 24.5 million. At 18%, annual tax 4.41 million; established credited advances 3 million leave 1.41 million. No second deduction of the same depreciation/loss. [110–113, 121, 123, 125, 130][code]

```oa-check
name: Armenia ordinary corporate book to tax bridge
inputs:
  book_profit: 30000000
  public_tax_fine: 500000
  book_depreciation: 3000000
  established_tax_depreciation: 4000000
  eligible_prior_loss: 5000000
  credited_advances: 3000000
steps:
  - current_tax_result: book_profit + public_tax_fine + book_depreciation - established_tax_depreciation
  - prior_loss_used: min(eligible_prior_loss, max(current_tax_result, 0))
  - taxable_profit: max(current_tax_result - prior_loss_used, 0)
  - annual_tax: taxable_profit * 0.18
  - remaining_payment: max(annual_tax - credited_advances, 0)
expected:
  current_tax_result: 29500000
  taxable_profit: 24500000
  annual_tax: 4410000
  remaining_payment: 1410000
```

### 2. Representation: ordinary versus registration year

Annual gross income 200 million; established representation cost 1.8 million. Ordinary percentage cap is 1 million, below absolute cap 5 million: deduct 1 million, disallow 800,000. If instead the statutory registration-year exception is established, the 5-million absolute cap permits this 1.8-million cost. No special taxpayer facts are inferred. [116][code]

```oa-check
name: Armenia representation ordinary and registration year
inputs:
  gross_income: 200000000
  qualifying_cost: 1800000
steps:
  - ordinary_deduction: min(qualifying_cost, gross_income * 0.005, 5000000)
  - ordinary_disallowance: qualifying_cost - ordinary_deduction
  - registration_year_deduction: min(qualifying_cost, 5000000)
expected:
  ordinary_deduction: 1000000
  ordinary_disallowance: 800000
  registration_year_deduction: 1800000
```

Qualifying production equipment original cost 30 million, lawful five-year term, six complete depreciation months in 2026: annual 6 million, current 3 million. Separate qualifying small depreciable asset cost 50,000 inclusive is fully deducted in acquisition year, no second ordinary depreciation. No incomplete month, improvement or special acceleration.   selected_years: 5
```oa-check
  complete_months: 6
  qualifying_small_asset_cost: 50000

  - current_equipment_depreciation: annual_equipment_depreciation * complete_months / 12
```

### 4. Loss expiry and oldest-first use

After current-year deductions, 2026 positive result 10 million. Ordinary verified unused 2021 loss 8 million is in its fifth following tax year; 2023 loss 6 million remains eligible. Use 8 million then 2 million, leaving 2023 balance 4 million. A separate 2020 balance expired before 2026 and is excluded; no special-regime pause or reorganisation. [123(1)(4)][code]

```oa-check

inputs:
  current_result_after_current_deductions: 10000000
  eligible_loss_2021: 8000000
  eligible_loss_2023: 6000000
steps:
```

# Armenia corporate cross-border preparation v0.1

## Who this applies to

Use this Guide for ordinary corporate 2026 cross-border receipts/payments and associated residence evidence. It is a working-paper method, not a certificate of treaty entitlement. Domestic rules come first; a ratified treaty and its current protocol/MLI, where applicable, require their own analysis. This draft does not establish any bilateral treaty rate, PE exception or relief-at-source/refund procedure. [Code Articles 2, 19(7)][code]

Resident organisations are those located in Armenia, with organisation location defined by state registration; do not replace this statutory test with an invented universal place-of-effective-management rule. Resident profit taxpayers bring Armenian and foreign income into the tax base; nonresident corporate profit taxpayers are taxed on Armenian-source income, with separate PE and no-PE bases. Individual entrepreneurs, investment funds and other special regimes require their own classification rather than automatic application of the ordinary corporate rate. [22–23, 103–105, 125][code]

For individual residence screening, Article 25 has the 183-or-more-days test, counting both arrival and departure days, and independent vital-interests/state-service limbs. If resident on a day under the stated limbs, the Code treats the person as resident for the entire tax year. Fewer than 183 days alone does not prove nonresidence. This is screening only: personal income categories, payroll, pension/social obligations and treaty dual-residence allocation are not computed by the corporate withholding table below. [25][code]

### Establish the PE and registration position

Article 27(1) lists places of business including production, management, extraction, construction, branch/representative operations and specified joint activity. Several listed activities do not have a universal 183-day grace period. The separate services/work limb in paragraph 2 uses at least 183 calendar days in a tax year and related-project rules. Exhibition/fair goods sales have a separate more-than-30-day rule. Preparatory/support relief has its own conditions, direct-beneficiary requirement and less-than-three-year period. Dependent agents and joint activity need distinct tests. [27(1)–(5), (9)–(10)][code]

Paragraphs 7–8 distinguish activity characteristics, tax registration and the statutory calculation/payment consequence of an unregistered PE-like operation. No registration does not prove no PE risk. Conversely, do not claim that registration alone resolves treaty attribution. Retain contracts, actual conduct, staff/project days, premises, authority, registration date and income documents. The former paragraph 6 labour-supply rule was repealed by HO-377-N, effective after its December 2025 publication; do not use an older English consolidation to claim a blanket labour-supply PE exception in 2026. [27][code]; [HO-377-N Articles 1, 7][pe-amend]

## Rates, bands and thresholds

Ordinary domestic rules before separately established treaty/Code relief:

| Population/receipt | Rate or test | Tax year and primary source |
|---|---|---|
| Ordinary resident corporate profit / attributable PE profit | 18% on established taxable profit | 2026, [125(1)][code] |
| No-PE insurance indemnities, reinsurance fees and freight | 5% | 2026, [125(4)(1)][code] |
| No-PE passive income, subject to specific exceptions | 10% | 2026, [125(4)(2)][code] |
| No-PE dividends | 5% | 2026, [125(4)(3.1)][code] |
| Specified securities capital appreciation / stated participation exception | Statute distinguishes 0% securities appreciation and 18% appreciation on the stated stocks/shares/units in another organisation | 2026, [125(4)(4)][code]; actual instrument classification required |
| Other Armenian-source no-PE income outside the preceding categories | 20% | 2026, [125(4)(5)][code] |
| Relevant listed-jurisdiction goods advance without outcome | Statutory deemed-income event on day 366 after payment where the 365-day condition is met | 2026, [125(6)][code]; list/status/outcome must be established |

Do not apply corporate interest/royalty withholding rates to an individual. Do not claim all securities are exempt or every participation gain is taxed on gross proceeds. Treaty relief, exempt-income provisions, beneficial receipt, instrument and recipient status must be resolved for the particular transaction. The examples assume no relief and ordinary established corporate scope. [103–105, 107–108, 125][code]

**Future gate:** HO-385-N amends bank-dividend treatment, related distribution wording and reporting/payment provisions. Article 14 generally starts those amendments on **1 February 2027**, with a separate expense provision effective earlier. It also reaches dividends distributed/paid from earlier-period profits. Neither July enactment nor an earlier profit year makes the future 15% bank-dividend rate current for an October 2026 event. Recheck the complete transition and later implementing instruments for 2027. [HO-385-N Articles 2, 4–7, 14][dividend-amend]

## The base

### Classify the source before the rate

Article 107 determines source under the profit-tax rules, separately from VAT place of supply. Goods, actual work/services, intermediary activities, property, transport/post, telecoms, audit and passive receipts have different connecting factors. Interest/royalty and dividend payer connections are not interchangeable with the place where a supplier's staff sit. Armenian real-property rent is expressly sourced by property location. Inseparable work/service income can be fully Armenian-source under the stated rule, rather than apportioned by an arbitrary percentage. [107][code]

Offshore consultancy, legal, accounting, management, expert, marketing, advertising, translation, engineering and similar services can be Armenian-source under paragraph 4. **From 1 July 2026**, HO-234-N Article 20 broadens that paragraph's recipient language to a resident organisation, Armenia-registered individual entrepreneur or the stated nonresident PE. Do not use the older English phrase limited to a resident profit taxpayer to omit a payment merely because the Armenian recipient uses a special regime. An unrelated offshore supplier is not automatically exempt. Actual treaty business-profits/PE and domestic relief remain separate, unverified questions here. [107(4)][code]; [HO-234-N Articles 20, 31][july-amend]

Nonresident capital appreciation has document-specific initial/book/revalued-value rules in Article 107(3)(5); absent the specified evidence, the statute can treat the entire alienation value as appreciation. No reconstructed acquisition cost without documents. Full asset/security/immovable-property, related-party and treaty methods remain open, so no property-gain return is certified here. [107(3)(5), 125(4)(4)][code]

### Separate attributable PE profit from other receipts

For an ordinary registered corporate PE, Article 105(1)(3) uses taxable profit with applicable deductions, and Article 133 requires separated accounting and settlement-document identification of the PE for deductible expense. A head-office charge is not deductible just because a group spreadsheet allocates it. Pricing, actual benefit and current deduction restrictions require further evidence. [105, 110, 133][code]; [companion TP method](am-transfer-pricing.md)

Article 125(1)/(5) ties attribution to the PE's supporting income documents, regardless of merely naming/not naming the PE as receiver in a contract. Non-attributed receipts have a separate gross-income/rate route. Article 132(4) separately addresses nonresident dividends regardless of attribution. Keep a receipt-by-receipt attribution register, then reconcile any tax-agent withholding credits under Article 130 rather than taxing the same receipt twice. The example below assumes the attribution and allowable costs already established; it does not verify every deduction. [105, 125, 130, 132–133][code]

### Payment events and gross/net agreement

Article 132 withholding operates on payment events, including part payments, property, set-off, restructuring/novation, specified claim assignment/waiver and the Article 109(3)(5) dividend-distribution decision. Cash leaving a bank is not the only trigger. From July 2026, HO-234-N Article 27 changes claim-assignment wording and clarifies the waiver event; use current Armenian text. Returned payments have paragraph-3 timing/corrected-report conditions, not automatic erasure of a filed liability. [109, 132][code]; [HO-234-N 27, 31][july-amend]

For a contract whose taxable amount is established as gross, withholding = gross × applicable rate and net = gross − withholding. If the agreement instead guarantees the recipient a net amount and the payer bears tax, first establish its legal/contractual character and tax base; under the examples' single-rate assumptions gross = net / (1 − rate). This is algebra under an assumed taxable gross base, not a statutory election or proof all payer-borne taxes are deductible. [105, 125, 132][code]

### Resident foreign-tax relief

Article 20 includes foreign taxable objects and permits reduction for corresponding taxes collected abroad under foreign law, capped at Armenian tax on those foreign objects calculated under the Code. Separate the foreign income/deduction/base reconciliation, comparable tax and collection evidence, currency/period and any treaty restriction. Do not credit VAT, penalties or an unsupported foreign assessment as corporate profit tax. Actual tax equivalence and multi-country/category allocation need the underlying instruments. [20, 130(1)(2)][code]

**Two limits are different.** First calculate the Article 20(3) foreign-object cap; foreign tax above that cap is not automatically eligible carryforward. Then compare the legally deductible amount with the year's corresponding tax liability. Article 20(4) carries the deductible amount exceeding that annual liability into subsequent reporting years of the same tax type. Do not label all excess foreign tax refundable or carryable. Current return fields, ordering with other credits/prepayments, multi-year use and foreign adjustments remain to be reconciled before filing. [20(2)–(4), 130–131][code]

## Deadlines and filing

| Obligation | Statutory date/clock | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Tax agent's nonresident-income return | By the 20th inclusive of the month following the reporting quarter | [134(2)][code] |
| Tax agent's nonresident withholding payment | By the 20th inclusive of the month following the payment quarter | [136(2)][code] |
| Ordinary resident/PE annual profit-tax return and payment | By 20 April inclusive of the following tax year | [134(1), 136(1)][code] |
| No-PE nonresident without a tax agent | Annual return by 20 April following the reporting year; statutory filing unit is the authority serving Yerevan Kentron district; relevant tax payment by that date | [134(3), 136(3)][code] |

Keep the underlying payment event, income attribution, reporting quarter and annual period separate. These are statutory dates before any separately established extension/calendar adjustment; actual 2026/2027 filing acceptance, form numbers/rows, current office routing and acknowledgements have not been obtained. Do not turn a quarterly return into a monthly rule or defer ordinary withholding calculation to the return date. PE instalments under Article 135 need their own current computation and exemptions; this Guide does not certify them. [132, 134–136][code]

### Armenian residence evidence

Current Article 314 provides electronic applications/certification, including qualifying foreign-country forms, separate years/countries and Armenian certificates with English/Russian on request. It distinguishes the organisation/registered-entrepreneur route from other individuals, including the latter's vital-interests evidence, and category-specific immediate/two-working-day processing provisions. Those legal clocks do not establish that a particular incomplete application was accepted. [314][code]; [HO-377-N 6–7][pe-amend]

Actual 345-N as revised by 1629-N has Form 1 for organisations/individual entrepreneurs, Form 2 for individuals and Form 3 certificate. Reconcile TIN/legal name, tax year, destination country, identity/status grounds, supporting explanation and any foreign form. Certificate QR/control code, tax year and country must match the intended use. An Armenian certificate supports Armenian residence evidence; it is not a foreign recipient's certificate or blanket treaty relief. The SRC foreign-citizen service page describes that specific application route; do not apply it as every corporate process. No login, submission or issued certificate was obtained here. [314][code]; [345-N forms][certificate]; [SRC service][service]

## Penalties and interest

Article 401 ordinary tax late-payment interest is 0.075% per overdue day, within its scope and 730-day maximum. Article 402 provides a late-return fine based on 5% of the relevant calculated tax for each completed 15-day period, subject to its calculation stop and total-tax cap. Article 403 provides ordinary under-declaration sanctions of 50%, or 100% for its specified recurrence, with express exceptions. Do not stack these automatically or reuse transfer-pricing documentation sanctions as nonresident-return fines. Establish the exact offence, tax-agent liability, original due date, service, correction and applicable exceptions. [401–403][code]

The former PE staff-supply treatment, missing noncash withholding events and unjustified treaty relief are material classification risks. Full administrative-offence rules, amended-return relief, audit limitation, service/appeal/suspension deadlines, refunds and enforcement are not cleared by these numeric summaries. Do not invent an appeal period. [27, 54, 132, 401–403][code]

## Cross-border points

Before any treaty conclusion obtain the actual treaty and protocol, operative year, covered taxes/persons, residence and tie-breaker provisions, payment article, PE/business-profits interaction and any applicable anti-abuse/MLI provisions. Article 19(7) delegates treaty-benefit procedure to the Government; current relief-at-source/refund instruments have not been reconciled here. No treaty count, beneficial-owner ruling, residence certificate alone or generic treaty model establishes exemption. [2, 19, 20, 27][code]

Personal migration/foreign salary, foreign pensions, social-security coordination, emigration/exit, business restructuring, CFC/anti-avoidance, specialised property/security gains and EAEU VAT/customs remain coverage gaps. Do not infer that no rule applies from their omission. Armenia's corporate no-PE table does not replace these methods or the retained personal/payroll Guides' required current-law reconstruction.

## Worked examples that recompute

All amounts are hypothetical AMD. Corporate recipient/scope, source, no relief and the stated dates/classification are assumed established. Examples are workpapers, not accepted filings.

### 1. Ordinary no-PE corporate royalty

October 2026 Armenian tax agent pays an established gross royalty of 10 million to a foreign company without an attributable PE. No treaty/domestic relief. At the 10% passive-income rate, withholding is 1 million and recipient net 9 million. Report/payment follow the quarter; an individual royalty requires separate PIT analysis. [107(3), 125(4)(2), 132, 134, 136][code]

```oa-check
name: Armenia corporate royalty gross withholding
inputs:
  gross_royalty: 10000000
steps:
  - withholding: gross_royalty * 0.10
  - recipient_net: gross_royalty - withholding
expected:
  withholding: 1000000
  recipient_net: 9000000
```

### 2. Offshore consultancy with a net guarantee

October 2026 offshore consultancy for an Armenian resident organisation, nonresident corporate supplier/no attributable PE. Source and 20% other-income category established; no relief. Contract guarantees 4 million net and payer bears the single withholding tax: taxable gross 5 million, tax 1 million. Merely multiplying the net by 20% would understate the assumed gross-base tax. Actual contractual/tax-on-tax classification and payer deductibility need separate review. [107(4), 125(4)(5), 132][code]; [HO-234-N 20][july-amend]

```oa-check
name: Armenia conditional consultancy net guarantee
inputs:
  guaranteed_net: 4000000
  established_rate: 0.20
steps:
  - taxable_gross: guaranteed_net / (1 - established_rate)
  - withholding: taxable_gross * established_rate
  - net_check: taxable_gross - withholding
expected:
  taxable_gross: 5000000
  withholding: 1000000
  net_check: 4000000
```

### 3. Qualifying dividend decision before cash transfer

October 2026 qualifying Article 109(3)(5) decision distributing 2 million gross from reporting-year profits to a nonresident company, no relief. Article 132(2)(7) treats the decision as a payment event: 5% withholding 100,000 and residual entitlement 1.9 million, even if cash is transferred later. This does not apply the future bank-dividend changes or settle interim/nonstandard distributions. [109, 125(4)(3.1), 132][code]; [HO-385-N 14][dividend-amend]

```oa-check
name: Armenia established dividend decision tax event
inputs:
  established_gross_dividend: 2000000
steps:
  - withholding: established_gross_dividend * 0.05
  - residual_entitlement: established_gross_dividend - withholding
expected:
  withholding: 100000
  residual_entitlement: 1900000
```

### 4. Foreign-object cap is not unlimited carryforward

Ordinary resident company: established foreign taxable profit 30 million and domestic taxable profit 20 million, no other relief/prepayment. At 18%, total Armenian tax 9 million and foreign-object cap 5.4 million. Corresponding foreign tax actually collected is 7 million: deductible credit 5.4 million, Armenian balance 3.6 million. The 1.6 million above the foreign-object cap is not an Article 20(4) carryforward merely because it was paid abroad. [20, 125(1), 130][code]

```oa-check
name: Armenia foreign object tax credit limitation
inputs:
  foreign_taxable_profit: 30000000
  domestic_taxable_profit: 20000000
  corresponding_foreign_tax_collected: 7000000
steps:
  - total_armenian_tax: (foreign_taxable_profit + domestic_taxable_profit) * 0.18
  - foreign_object_cap: foreign_taxable_profit * 0.18
  - deductible_credit: min(corresponding_foreign_tax_collected, foreign_object_cap)
  - armenian_balance: total_armenian_tax - deductible_credit
  - foreign_tax_above_object_cap: corresponding_foreign_tax_collected - deductible_credit
expected:
  total_armenian_tax: 9000000
  deductible_credit: 5400000
  armenian_balance: 3600000
  foreign_tax_above_object_cap: 1600000
```

### 5. Eligible credit exceeds the annual liability

Assume after all legal base and corresponding-tax tests, Article 20(3) eligible credit is 5.4 million, while the year's established corresponding tax liability is only 4 million because of other results. With no competing credits/prepayments, use 4 million this year, carry 1.4 million under Article 20(4), current residual zero. This is a different limit from example 4; neither example resolves multi-country ordering or the actual future return. [20(3)–(4)][code]

```oa-check
name: Armenia eligible foreign credit annual liability carryforward
inputs:
  established_eligible_credit: 5400000
  established_annual_liability: 4000000
steps:
  - current_use: min(established_eligible_credit, established_annual_liability)
  - eligible_carryforward: max(established_eligible_credit - current_use, 0)
  - current_residual: max(established_annual_liability - current_use, 0)
expected:
  current_use: 4000000
  eligible_carryforward: 1400000
  current_residual: 0
```

### 6. PE profit and non-attributed service receipt

Ordinary registered corporate PE has 50 million documented attributable revenue and 35 million already-established allowable deductions: profit 15 million, tax 2.7 million. The same nonresident separately receives 5 million Armenian-source service income not attributed to the PE, under an established 20% no-relief category: tax 1 million. Separate computed amounts total 3.7 million before actual credits/prepayments and return reconciliation. Do not deduct PE costs again from the 5-million gross non-attributed receipt. [105, 125(1)/(5), 130, 132–133][code]

```oa-check
name: Armenia PE and non attributed income separation
inputs:
  attributable_revenue: 50000000
  established_allowable_pe_costs: 35000000
  non_attributed_service_gross: 5000000
steps:
  - pe_taxable_profit: max(attributable_revenue - established_allowable_pe_costs, 0)
  - pe_computed_tax: pe_taxable_profit * 0.18
  - non_attributed_computed_tax: non_attributed_service_gross * 0.20
  - combined_computed_tax_before_credits: pe_computed_tax + non_attributed_computed_tax
expected:
  pe_taxable_profit: 15000000
  pe_computed_tax: 2700000
  non_attributed_computed_tax: 1000000
  combined_computed_tax_before_credits: 3700000
```

# Armenia tax overview v0.2

## Start with the taxpayer and activity

Armenia's tax year is the calendar year. The State Revenue Committee administers tax filings. Begin by identifying whether the taxpayer is an individual, individual entrepreneur, resident commercial organisation, non-resident with Armenian-source income or a permanent establishment. Then classify the receipt and activity, check source and residence, and test any special regime before applying a headline rate. The individual entrepreneur's business income does not automatically use the ordinary personal 20% method. [Tax Code, Articles 11, 13, 20, 103 and 140](https://www.arlis.am/hy/acts/215611/latest)

The Armenian dram (AMD) is the currency used in the domestic tax rules. Residence, source, treaty relief, permanent establishment, tax-agent duties and the correct tax base depend on the actual facts. Use the relevant method below; this overview does not determine those facts. [Tax Code](https://www.arlis.am/hy/acts/215611/latest)

## Main routes

| Question | Starting point | Use this method |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Individual salary, passive income, property or annual declaration | Category-specific PIT rules; ordinary employment income is generally taxed at 20% | [Individual income tax](armenia-income-tax.md) |
| Resident company or Armenian permanent establishment | Ordinary profit tax is generally 18%, subject to the taxpayer, base, deductions and special rules | [Corporate income tax](am-corporate-income-tax.md) |
| Goods or services subject to VAT | Ordinary VAT rate is 20%; registration, place, exemptions, recovery and timing still matter | [VAT](armenia-vat.md) |
| Resident business considering a special regime | Check business form, prior or expected turnover, activity, exclusions and election deadline | [Tax planning](armenia-tax-optimization.md) |
| Employer or payer making individual payments | Keep PIT withholding separate from pension, stamp and health contributions | [Payroll](armenia-payroll.md) and [social contributions](armenia-social-contributions.md) |
| Cross-border company, owner or related party | Establish source, permanent establishment, withholding, treaty and credit treatment | [Corporate cross-border](am-cross-border.md) and [transfer pricing](am-transfer-pricing.md) |

Ordinary corporate profit tax returns and payment are generally due by 20 April after the tax year. The annual individual declaration has different dates for the transition year: the 2025-income declaration window is 2 March through 1 November 2026; the general 2026-income window is 2 March through 1 July 2027. The latter date applies to the declaration population and rules in the Code, not as a universal filing obligation for every person. Check the individual's filing status and any amended deadline before using it. [Tax Code, Articles 125, 156 and 158](https://www.arlis.am/hy/acts/215611/latest); [HO-76-N](https://www.arlis.am/hy/acts/206337)

The headline rates above are signposts, not a computation. This map does not settle the taxpayer's residence, source, classification, VAT status, special regime, treaty protection, deductions or filing obligation. It does not catalogue every tax, duty, municipal charge, customs rule, exemption, refund, licence or sector-specific obligation. # Armenia transfer-pricing preparation v0.1

## Who this applies to

Use this method for the 2026 tax year after identifying the taxpayer, actual transactions and applicable law. Chapter 73 addresses profit tax and natural-resource utilisation royalty. It does not supply a general VAT valuation adjustment. Article 360(3) excludes transactions with the stated public/local bodies, Central Bank, regulated tariffs and transactions with tax-base peculiarities prescribed by ratified treaties. Test exclusions before aggregating. [Code Articles 360–363][code]

Article 362 covers direct/indirect participation of at least 20% and practical control, including common control. Ownership alone is insufficient screening: also check voting rights/board formation, financing or guarantees exceeding 51% of opening assets, the specified more-than-80% income/expense dependencies with their exclusions, joint activity, gratuitous use and actual management. Record the exact limb, percentage denominator and measurement date. [Article 362][code]

Article 363 distinguishes related resident/nonresident transactions; specified **resident/resident** transactions where one party is a natural-resource royalty payer or enjoys the relevant profit-tax/royalty benefit; transactions with persons registered in a liberal-tax jurisdiction even without relatedness; and head-office/Armenian-PE dealings and expense allocation. Article 361's liberal-tax definition includes the stated 10%-or-lower/exemption tests, including person-specific regimes. Establish the counterparty's actual regime rather than making a country-name assumption. Specific regulated financial services in Article 363(5) are uncontrolled; this is not an exemption for every intercompany loan. [Articles 361–363][code]

**Translation check:** the English reproduction's Article 363(2) incorrectly repeats resident/nonresident wording. The Armenian text says related resident persons. Its Article 363(5) financial-services cross-reference also differs. Use the Armenian provision and actual underlying financial-service classification. The current consolidation includes later 2026 changes elsewhere; the English version is supporting translation, not a complete current-law substitute. [Armenian Code][code]; [English translation][english]

## Rates, bands and thresholds

| Item | Statutory amount/test | Period and source |
|---|---|---|
| Participation limb | At least 20%; practical control can apply independently | 2026, [362][code] |
| Chapter 73 annual application | All controlled transactions exceed AMD 200 million, excluding VAT, excise and environmental tax | 2026, [363(6)][code] |
| Annual notification | Exceeds AMD 200 million on its separate population, excluding Article 363(4) PE/head-office transactions | 2026, [375(1)][code] |
| Liberal-tax definition | Stated 10%-or-lower profit-tax rate or exemption, including qualifying person-specific regimes | 2026, [361(1)(5)][code] |
| Statutory country-report trigger | Parent organisation's prior-year gross revenue **exceeds** EUR 750 million | 2026 text, [376(1.1)(3)][code] |

The 200-million test is strict: equality does not exceed it. The general application and notification populations differ; do not remove PE/head-office transactions from both merely because Article 375 excludes them from notification. Loan principal/interest valuation, foreign-exchange dates, repeated balances and unusual transactions require classification under the Code and current instructions before aggregation. No blanket netting of sales against purchases. A proposal for a higher threshold or later deadline is not operative law verified here. [Articles 16, 363, 375][code]; [notification instructions][notice]

## The base

### Establish the transaction and method

Reconcile contracts with actual conduct, counterparties, ledger flows and segmentation. Article 373 gives actual transactions priority where their content differs from the contract. Prepare the Article 365 functions/assets/risks analysis, product/service/financing/intangible characteristics, contractual terms, market circumstances and business strategy. A comparability adjustment under Article 366 needs reliable information and an explanation of how it improves comparability. [Articles 365–366, 373][code]

Select the most appropriate method from CUP, resale price, cost-plus, transactional net margin and profit split. Use CUP when it and another method are equally reliable; internal comparables also take priority over external ones when equally reliable. More than one method is not mandatory. Select the simpler or more reliably benchmarked tested party for resale/cost-plus/net margin; a foreign tested party requires evidence, not automatic rejection. Do not use inaccessible tax-secret information as an undisclosed benchmark. [Articles 367–369][code]; [556-N points 3–15][methods]

| Method | Workpaper computation | Evidence needed |
|---|---|---|
| CUP | Comparable adjusted price × matched quantity | Actual comparability; a single comparable is sufficient only under the rule's full comparability conditions |
| Resale | Gross profit / net sales; implied purchase amount = sales × (1 − established margin) | Reseller functions, no material added value, consistent gross-cost classification |
| Cost-plus | Gross profit / relevant direct and indirect costs; remuneration = costs × (1 + established markup) | Consistent cost pool; do not substitute a sales margin for a cost markup |
| Net margin | Transaction-related net profit / appropriate costs, sales or assets | Segmented results, suitable denominator and accounting comparability; exclude unrelated income/expense |
| Profit split | Allocate established combined/residual profit on a supported economic basis | Highly integrated activities or valuable intangibles; no invented universal allocation percentage |

Sources: [Code Article 368][code]; [556-N method provisions][methods]. The example margins below are hypothetical already-supported benchmark inputs, not Armenian safe harbours or results of a real database search. Current-year data is the starting point; Article 370 permits its stated prior-year and up-to-three-prior-year circumstances. It does not prescribe a universal three-year weighted average for every taxpayer. Closely linked transactions can be combined under Article 372 when separate analysis is unreliable. [Articles 370, 372][code]

### Range and adjustment

853-N point 3 uses the full minimum–maximum range where all observations are reliable uncontrolled comparables. Where point 4's reliability condition applies after comparability adjustments, sort the observations, keeping duplicates as separate entries. For the lower/upper bounds calculate n × 0.25 / n × 0.75: an integer position uses the arithmetic mean of that observation and the next; a fractional position uses the observation at the next whole position. Do not substitute a spreadsheet's default percentile interpolation. The Code's median is the middle observation for odd n and the mean of the middle pair for even n. [853-N points 3–4][range]; [Article 361(1)(15)][code]

Article 371 permits authority adjustment of an out-of-range indicator to the median, with its stated burden of proof; the taxpayer must support a different proposed indicator. Article 364 deals with additional profit-tax base/reduction of tax loss and royalty base, and contains separate restrictions on recalculating reporting-period liabilities/advances and the domestic natural-resource-royalty case. Keep the pricing/base bridge separate from tax due, contractual settlements and corresponding relief. Do not apply a universal 18% multiplier or amend historic CIT/advance returns automatically. Full current TP calculation-form implementation of that bridge remains open here. [Articles 364, 371, 374][code]

## Deadlines and filing

| Event | Statutory clock | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Controlled-transaction notification | By 20 April inclusive of the following tax year; for 2026, statutory date 20 April 2027 before any separately established extension/calendar rule | [375(3)][code] |
| Local/master information requested | 30 working days after receipt of written notification | [376(2)][code] |
| Additional requested information | 10 working days after receipt | [376(2)][code] |
| Requested interview arrangements | Provide venue/time/participant information within 5 working days after receipt | [376(2)][code] |
| Armenian translation requested for English/Russian documents | 10 working days after receipt | [376(3)][code] |
| Statutory country report | Within the 12 months immediately following each tax-year end | [376(2)][code] |

Notification, documentation and TP tax calculation are distinct outputs. Article 375 permits self-corrected notifications before receipt of the documentation request. If the authority detects wrong/missing transaction information, its notification and the taxpayer's corrected notification/objection have separate 10- and 30-working-day clocks. Both parties notify qualifying domestic transactions. Keep service/receipt proof and a working-day calendar; do not count every clock as ordinary calendar days. [375][code]

The actual 671-N notification consolidation incorporates 948-N amendments and is identified as applicable from 1 January 2026. Its instructions require **electronic-only** notification. Map identity/TIN/year/contact in Part 1, resident/nonresident selection in 1.1, nonresident controlled transactions in Part 2 and domestic controlled transactions in Part 5; both parts apply if both populations exist. Parts 2.1–2.4 and 5.1–5.4 collect goods/loans/intangibles/claim-transfer detail. Part 4 records internal uncontrolled transactions; Part 6 records activity codes and proportions. Loan supplementary fields distinguish opening/closing principal and payable interest, rather than treating all fields as a second transaction total. Amounts are AMD under the referenced Article 16 conversion rules. Actual login/schema, rounding, validation errors and accepted filing have not been tested. [671-N form and instructions, especially 1, 6.1, 14–18, 27–31, 35–45][notice]

Prepare local documentation with business/economic context, transactions and functional analysis, method selection, counterparties/residence, comparable sources, applicable range and tested-party financial information. Article 376 separately describes parent/master and country-report information and permits requests to PEs. Do not assert that Armenia has no master-file/CbCR rules because an older international summary says so. Current implementing forms, group attribution/currency/exchange mechanics and actual filing obligations for a particular parent remain to be reconciled before filing. [376][code]

## Penalties and interest

The current Armenian Article 402.1 provides organisation notification fines of AMD 1 million where prior-year gross income does not exceed AMD 1 billion, AMD 3 million for the over-1-billion band, and AMD 5 million for over AMD 2 billion. Read the upper band first. Wrong/missing information after the specified written correction process can attract AMD 500,000 per error/missing transaction under paragraphs 2–3; it is not an automatic charge for any innocent draft typo. [402.1][code]

Article 402.2 charges 10% of each documentation-subject controlled transaction's value for failure to provide documentation by the required deadline. If still not provided within 30 days after the fine is imposed, it provides 0.04% per overdue day on that transaction value. Do not confuse this with ordinary tax late-payment interest or recalculate its base as only the proposed TP adjustment. The exact service, first overdue day, assessed transaction population and procedural remedies need the actual notice/act. [402.2][code]

Article 401 ordinary tax late-payment interest is 0.075% a day, capped at 730 days under its stated scope. Article 374 has special TP interest treatment: independently calculated adjustments, authority study/proposal and inspection have different starting consequences. The Armenian provision for independent adjustments says no **late-payment interest** is calculated; this is not blanket immunity from all fines or other offences. Full applicable assessment, appeal, suspension and settlement mechanics remain open. [374, 401][code]

## Cross-border points

Analyse PE/head-office dealings separately from annual notification, while retaining Article 376's PE documentation request power. Withholding, deductibility, customs and VAT are separate from the pricing calculation. An adjustment does not prove a foreign corresponding deduction/refund. Article 377 provides MAP where an effective treaty exists; Article 378 permits an application for an advance pricing agreement for transactions with nonresident related parties. Actual treaty, competent-authority procedure, deadlines and current APA conditions require their own primary instruments. No bilateral treaty/MLI or granted agreement is verified in this Guide. [363–364, 376–378][code]

### 2. CUP sales shortfall

Assume the annual gate is separately met, matched goods/terms and a reliable adjusted uncontrolled price of AMD 12,000 per unit versus charged AMD 10,000 for 10,000 units. ```oa-check

```oa-check
inputs:
  quantity: 10000
  charged_unit_price: 10000
  supported_unit_price: 12000
steps:

  - supported_revenue: quantity * supported_unit_price
  - positive_revenue_difference: max(supported_revenue - charged_revenue, 0)
```

### 3. Cost markup denominator

Established comparable cost pool 80 million and hypothetical supported gross markup 10%; remuneration 88 million. Charged 84 million implies 5%, giving a 4-million remuneration difference.   cost_pool: 80000000
```oa-check
  benchmark_markup: 0.10
  charged_revenue: 84000000
steps:
  - benchmark_profit: cost_pool * benchmark_markup
  - benchmark_revenue: cost_pool + benchmark_profit
  - actual_markup: (charged_revenue - cost_pool) / cost_pool
  - remuneration_difference: benchmark_revenue - charged_revenue
expected:
  benchmark_revenue: 88000000
  actual_markup: 0.05
  remuneration_difference: 4000000
```

### 4. Resale sales margin

Established resale facts: net sales 150 million, controlled purchase 130 million, supported gross sales margin 20%. Implied purchase amount 120 million and purchase difference 10 million. No material added value or inconsistent cost classification; no universal deemed margin. [368][code]; [556-N 26–30][methods]

```oa-check
  charged_purchase: 130000000
  supported_margin: 0.20

  - purchase_difference: max(charged_purchase - implied_purchase, 0)
```

Assume 853-N point 4 applies to eight sorted observations: 2%, 3%, 4%, 5%, 6%, 7%, 8%, 9%. Positions 2 and 6 are integers: lower bound (3% + 4%)/2 = 3.5%; upper (7% + 8%)/2 = 7.5%. # Armenia individual income tax preparation v0.2

## Who this applies to

Prepare 2026 personal-income-tax workpapers for resident/nonresident individuals, keeping the separate 2025 declaration filed in 2026 clearly identified. Article 140 treats individual entrepreneurs/notaries as PIT taxpayers for personal income; their entrepreneurial income is not automatically the ordinary personal 20% base. Business profit/turnover/micro regimes need their own methods. [Code Articles 140–143][code]; [corporate/regime screening](am-corporate-income-tax.md)

Article 25 residence includes 183 or more days, arrival/departure days, vital interests and the stated state-service limb. Fewer days do not alone establish nonresidence. Residence under the specified limbs on a day produces whole-tax-year domestic residence. Residents bring domestic/foreign personal income into scope; nonresidents bring Armenian-source income subject to Article 141's exceptions. Citizenship, immigration residence permission and tax residence are separate inputs. [25, 140–144][code]

Classify source under Article 144, including Armenian payer/PE employment and civil contracts, passive-income connections and the nonresident employer/PE staff provision. Tax residence alone does not settle a treaty tie-breaker or foreign payroll/social obligation. Obtain the actual treaty, period and certificates before using a treaty conclusion. [20, 25, 107, 141, 144][code]; [cross-border method](am-cross-border.md)

## The base

### Classify each receipt and event

Maintain a ledger by person, source, category, period, payer/tax-agent status, accrual/payment event, gross/noncash value, legal exemption, taxable base, rate, withholding and declaration treatment. Article 142 uses accrual for stated salary/other categories and cash rules for passive/civil-contract/other receipts, with special conversion and noncash events. Its July 2026 paragraph 2 imports Article 132(2)'s event rules **except the corporate dividend-decision limb**. Do not copy the corporate decision-before-cash example into personal dividend PIT. [142, 132][code]; [HO-234-N Article 28][july]

Article 143 deducts the legally non-taxable income in Article 147, not a general business-expense allowance from every personal receipt. A loan receipt, account transfer, gift, sale, pension, salary and service fee are different facts. Reconcile documentary origin before treating a bank credit as taxable income or exempt capital. Personal spending and corporate depreciation are not universal PIT deductions. [140–147][code]

Article 147 includes particular benefits, pensions under its stated domestic/foreign pension-law scope, gifts/inheritances from natural persons with exceptions, and specified property receipts. Voluntary-pension receipts have separate treatment. Its private-person property-sale rule has developer/crypto exceptions, and land has its own provision. Verify the exact asset, seller/purchaser status, documentation and anti-substitution facts; do not claim all gifts, property gains or foreign retirement receipts are always exempt. [147(1), (2), (13), (16), (16.1), (38), 150(3)–(4)][code]

Article 149 securities exemptions depend on instrument, listing/date and income character. Exceptions include payment instruments, remuneration disguised as securities, specified property-backed participations sold within the statutory period and ordinary dividends. A broker statement or the word capital gain alone does not establish exemption. No hypothetical listing or universal zero capital-gains rate. Full instrument, crypto, developer/pledged-property and special foreign-pension implementation remains open. [145–150][code]

### Rent and withholding reconciliation

Calculate ordinary rent PIT and separately aggregate all annual received rent for the AMD 60-million excess test, including tax-agent rent. The extra 10% applies only to the excess, on top of ordinary 10%, not 20% on the whole year's rent. Reconcile tax already withheld so the annual calculation does not levy the same basic 10% twice. Rental registration/notification, related-use, special valuations and current form acceptance still need their own evidence. [150(7), 152, 156][code]; [300-N Annex 3, row 3.11][form]

Article 150(13) has a special 20% rule for the specified missing supporting documents, with an alternative-document exception containing identity and other requirements. It is not a default when a description is unfamiliar. Article 150(14)–(14.2) has delayed passive-income and conversion rules: cash basis does not mean tax can always be postponed indefinitely. Separate agent/no-agent and special bank/debt-interest exclusions. [150][code]

### Foreign tax and other levies

Article 20 permits corresponding foreign tax collected under foreign law, capped at Armenian tax on those foreign taxable objects. First establish source/category/exemption and matching tax, period and currency. Then distinguish the foreign-object cap from deductible credit exceeding the year's corresponding liability: only the latter has Article 20(4)'s subsequent-year route. Foreign tax above the object cap is not automatically carryable/refundable. Keep proof of collection and the foreign-authority-certified information required by the actual annual-form instructions. [20][code]; [300-N Annex 3 instructions, paragraph 11][form]

Mandatory pension, stamp and universal-health obligations are separate from personal PIT; a PIT calculation does not certify employee net pay or total annual liabilities. Their current status, bases and assessment/payment rules are open in the retained payroll/social Guides. Voluntary-pension deductions and social-expense reimbursement also have distinct statutory rules; do not deduct an assumed amount from salary because it appears as a bank debit. [147, 147.1, 158][code]
